text: Proposition thirty-seven creates a loan program for buyers
of qualifying new homes.
Assistance would be another loan, not free money.
The state housing finance agency could issue up
to twenty-five billion dollars in revenue bonds.
Homebuyers’ payments would repay investors and
administration.
That can reduce cash needed at closing, but
the family still owes the assistance loan as
well as its main mortgage.
A voter might support helping households with adequate
income
but too little saved cash.
If more buyers can bid while construction stays
constrained,
some benefit can be absorbed into higher prices.
Yes creates this loan program;
no leaves existing assistance options in place without
requiring the new program.
Visit our website for the fuller explanation,
source links, and official voter guide.
